title: 5. 时间的不完整性（incompleteness of time）

zh: 5. 时间的不完整性（incompleteness of time）

en: In the chapter of
devoted to ‘Analogies of Experience’, Kant seeks to clarify the manner in which we conceive of time in general, namely time as a unitary whole, the ‘substratum of all change’.

It is the presupposition of becoming, the field within which succession plays out: precisely for this reason, though, it does not change or pass by. Time-as-a-whole, characterised by permanence and immobility, ‘cannot be an object of perception’. In order to conceive it, we must

follow a transversal path and settle for an analogous image of it. It is the permanent ‘substratum of all change’ in empirical experience that indirectly gives account of permanent, unchanging time. According to Kant, this substratum present in phenomena – which lasts while everything else changes and passes by – is
And the only analogy that allows us to conceive the whole of time (which itself evades perception) is also to be found in substance – the invariant core of the objects that we perceive. Kant writes:
zh: 康德在《纯粹理性批判》讨论“经验类比”的章节中，试图澄清我们构想一般时间——即作为单一整体、“一切变化的基底”的时间——的方式。
它是生成变化的预设，是接续展开的场域；但恰恰因为如此，它自身不变化也不流逝。作为整体的时间以恒久和不动为特征，“不能成为知觉对象”。为了构想它，我们必须沿一条横向道路前进，满足于得到一个类比影像。经验中那个“一切变化的基底”——当其他一切都变化流逝时它始终持续——间接说明了恒久不变的时间。康德认为，现象中这个持续存在的基底就是实体。
于是，使我们能够构想时间整体——它自身逃避知觉——的唯一类比，也存在于实体之中，也就是我们所知觉对象的不变核心。康德写道：

en: the permanent is the

of our empirical representation of time itself; in it alone are relations of time possible … Permanence, as the abiding correlate of all existence of appearances, of all change and of all concomitance, expresses time in general. For change does not affect time itself, but only appearances in time.
zh: 恒久之物是我们关于时间本身的经验表象之基底；唯有在其中，时间关系才是可能的……恒久性作为现象的一切存在、一切变化和一切共存的持存对应项，表达一般时间。因为变化并不影响时间本身，只影响时间中的现象。

en: It is true enough that time as a unitary whole is permanent but does not itself change. And it is also true that we can only conceive its shape by way of analogy: by looking, that is, to an aspect of our own experience whose salient characteristic is precisely its permanence. But what is this aspect that offers us a perspicacious image of time in general – or better, of its persistence – when it displays its

unalterable character? All things considered, it is in answering this question that we find the decisive point. Unlike what Kant maintains, ‘the substratum of our empirical representation of time itself’ is in fact
, and not substance.
zh: 作为单一整体的时间确实恒久，自身却不变化。同样真实的是，我们只能通过类比来构想它的形式：也就是观察我们经验中某个以恒久为显著特征的面向。但究竟是哪一个面向在显示自身不可改变的性质时，为我们提供了一般时间——更准确地说，时间之持续——的清晰图景？归根结底，对这个问题的回答就是决定性环节。不同于康德的主张，“我们关于时间本身的经验表象之基底”事实上是潜能，而不是实体。

en: Both substance and potential are permanent: but in diametrically opposed ways. Since ‘the real … is always identical’, substance continues to subsist within each determinate ‘now’ as a perennial
. Since potential is never realised, it is, instead, perennially

, a not-now devoid of any date. And only this latter version of permanence appertains to time-as-a-whole. Indeed, if time-as-a-whole were actual, it would be possible to divide it into periods of greater or lesser length, and it would progress, thus rendering it indistinguishable from that which falls

time. Presence and totality stand in a relationship of mutual exclusion: time as a unitary whole, ‘the substratum of all change’, is an incessant not-now. We could even say that time-as-a-whole is always
: at odds with actuality, extraneous to any given ‘now’, never at one with any chronological perspective.
zh: 实体与潜能都恒久，但方式截然相反。由于“实在之物……始终同一”，实体作为永恒的在场继续存续于每个确定“现在”之中。潜能由于永远不被实现，却永远不处于现实态，是一个没有任何日期的非现在。只有后一种恒久才属于作为整体的时间。事实上，如果作为整体的时间成为现实态，它就能够被划分为长短不一的时期并不断推进，从而与落在时间中的东西无法区分。在场与总体相互排斥：作为单一整体、“一切变化的基底”的时间，就是一个永不停息的非现在。我们甚至可以说，作为整体的时间始终处于时代错置之中：它同现实性不合，外在于任何既定“现在”，从不与任何年代视角完全一致。

en: What does the expression ‘time-as-a-whole’ mean? What type of totality does time concern? Let us consider a piece of phenomenal evidence: time seems to be present only when it is not fully played out, when its realisation is still partial and incomplete. This phenomenal evidence is the indispensible presupposition for considering time-as-a-whole, though it is often unreflectively translated into according primacy to the chronological dimension of the future. This presupposition must be developed and amended in various different ways: such as to provoke a

. There is a strong but calamitous tendency to confuse the totality of time for its total completion, thus removing the ‘not’ from the intuitive formula ‘not completely realised’. Yet the very thing that we seek to comprehend in its totality is, by definition, incomplete: so when we speak of a complete whole, we are certainly
speaking about all time. The realisation that takes place here is the realisation of what falls
time: if we instead attributed this realisation to time-as-a-whole, we would only end up with a deeply
-temporal totality, as if the scourge of some mocking nemesis. So what different path must we follow in order to conceive the shape of the totality
time?
zh: “作为整体的时间”这一表达是什么意思？时间所涉及的是哪一种总体？让我们考察一项现象证据：时间似乎只有在尚未彻底展开、其现实化仍然部分而不完整时才在场。这项现象证据是思考作为整体之时间不可缺少的预设，尽管它常常未经反思便被翻译成赋予未来这一年代维度以首要地位。这个预设必须以多种方式得到发展和修正，以激起一种反应。人们有一种强烈却灾难性的倾向：把时间总体同时间彻底完成混为一谈，从而从“尚未完全实现”这一直观公式中删去“未”。然而，我们试图在其总体中理解的东西，按照定义就是不完整的；所以，当我们谈论一个完成了的整体时，所谈的当然不是全部时间。这里发生的实现，是落在时间中的东西的实现；如果反而把这种实现归给作为整体的时间，我们最后得到的只会是一种极端非时间的总体，仿佛遭到某个嘲弄人的复仇女神鞭打。那么，为了构想时间总体的形式，我们必须走哪一条不同道路？

en: The other possibility is that we unreservedly indulge (at least to start with) the phenomenal evidence that time is always incomplete. Here, the concept of totality must conform to its content, even at the cost of taking on paradoxical tones: the totality of the incomplete. We must consider as a unitary whole something that is
essentially incomplete, involute and unrealised. Time is a whole
it remains unrealised (and vice versa: it is unrealised
it constitutes a permanent and immutable whole). But in what sense can something incomplete

– something that cannot be completed – be called a whole? We can call it a whole, on one condition: that its lack of completion is not relative or provisional, but rather absolute and permanent; that its non-realisation does not concern only one ‘part’ of time, but precisely time-as-a-whole.

The intuitive formula ‘not completely realised’ must be corrected in a manner opposite to that which we just mentioned: it is the word ‘completely’ that we must remove, not the ‘not’. If we take the degree of realisation (or actuality) as our measure, then the totality of time appears as a negative, defective totality, to be conceived in terms of what is missing. Total time is unrealisable: it is never completed because it never even begins to be accomplished. Its permanence relies on its non-actuality: the two are inextricably bound together.
zh: 另一种可能，是我们毫无保留地顺从时间始终不完整这一现象证据——至少从这里开始。此时，总体概念必须适应其内容，即使为此带上悖论色彩：不完整者的总体。我们必须把某种本质上不完整、尚未展开且未实现的东西，当作单一整体来考察。时间作为一个整体存在，因为它仍未实现；反过来也一样：它之所以未实现，是因为它构成一个恒久不变的整体。然而，某种不完整、且无法完成的东西，在哪一种意义上可以称为整体？只有一个条件：它缺乏完成不是相对或暂时的，而是绝对而恒久的；它没有得到实现，不只是涉及时间的某个“部分”，而恰恰涉及作为整体的时间。
“尚未完全实现”这一直观公式必须以同前述做法相反的方式修正：需要删掉的不是“未”，而是“完全”。如果以实现（或现实性）程度为尺度，时间总体便显现为一种否定性的、有缺陷的总体，必须依据其所缺少之物来构想。总体时间不可实现：它从未完成，因为它甚至从未开始得到完成。它的恒久依赖它的非现实性；二者不可分割地联系在一起。

en: The totality of time is nothing other than the
. And this is why we can only comprehend this totality by way of analogy with our experience of potential. Time-as-a-whole is shaped like a
think, for example, of the capacity-to-speak, a whole without parts
which is permanently non-actual – and like the

think of the perceptible context for existence, always unformed and unrealised, the unalterable backdrop to chronological succession. Potential, the persistent not-now, ‘as the abiding correlate of all existence of appearances, of all change and of all concomitance, expresses time in general’.
zh: 时间总体不是别的，正是时间的潜在性（potentiality of time）。这就是为什么我们只能通过与潜能经验的类比来理解它。作为整体的时间，形如一种官能——例如言说能力，一个没有部分且恒久不处于现实态的整体——也形如世界——即存在的可感语境，永远没有形式、未被实现，是年代接续不可改变的背景。潜能，这个持续的非现在，“作为现象的一切存在、一切变化和一切共存的持存对应项，表达一般时间”。

en: Time-as-a-whole is not perceptible, because it is not present; and for the same reason, potential is also imperceptible. This poses the question as to whether it is

that best grasps the persistent non-actuality of each of this pair. We mentioned this question at the outset, though only later will we examine it properly. But at this point, halfway between mentioning the question and studying it in depth, it seems opportune to devote some initial remarks to it. Could it be that potential – this not-now thanks to which we can conceive the totality of time – escapes perception precisely because it appertains to memory? Could it be that faculties and the world (and, indirectly, time-as-a-whole) are something to which we must constantly
, something that we can only experience with a
gaze, something that we

? For now, a summary observation will have to suffice. We included memory among our ‘faculties, properly speaking’. Like all the others, it is a perpetual not-now. But unlike in the cases of the other faculties, the not-now is also memory’s own relevant field of application. Non-actuality is not just its mode of existence, but also the object of its attentions. That is to say, memory is concerned with the non-actuality of which potential in general consists: it reawakens it and informs us of it. As
such, faculties and the world (so too, by analogy, time-as-a-whole) are
objects of recollection and reminiscence. Memory should thus be considered a
, moreover, since it allows us to experience faculties and the world-context; because, in sum, it is the potential that maintains an open access-route to the other potentials.
zh: 作为整体的时间由于不在场而不可知觉；出于同一原因，潜能也不可知觉。这就提出一个问题：最能把握二者持续非现实性的，是否正是记忆？我们在开头提到过这个问题，不过要到后面才会正式考察。在提问与深入研究之间的这个中途位置，适宜先作几点初步说明。潜能——我们借以构想时间总体的非现在——之所以逃避知觉，是否恰恰因为它属于记忆？官能与世界（以及间接地，作为整体的时间）是否是我们必须不断返回的东西，是只能以回顾目光来经验、只能被记住的东西？眼下只能先作一项概要观察。我们把记忆列入“严格意义上的官能”；像其他官能一样，它是永恒的非现在。但不同于其他官能的是，非现在也是记忆自身相关的应用领域。非现实性不仅是它的存在方式，也是它关注的对象。也就是说，记忆关涉构成一般潜能的非现实性：它把这种非现实性重新唤醒，并向我们报告。因此，官能和世界——类比地说，也包括作为整体的时间——都是可记忆的，是回忆和追忆的对象。由此，记忆还应被视为一种元潜能（meta-potential），因为它使我们能够经验官能与世界—语境；简言之，它是那个维持通向其他潜能之开放道路的潜能。

en: However, there remains a striking difficulty – or at least an unresolved question – for the argumentation we have sketched out thus far. Memory engages with and portrays the not-now only if this latter appears to belong to the
. The radical non-actuality of potential is not sufficient to demonstrate that memory draws on it, since it is also necessary that this non-actuality take on the

of the past. Only the form, it should be understood: we are certainly not talking about a chronological ‘back then’. But even so, can it be legitimate to identify the not-now of a faculty as being a ‘before’ even if this ‘before’ is indefinite, dateless and in no sense possible to attach to any given present? To state that potential’s non-actuality has the traits of the past, and thus is memorable, means to assert the absolute (logical, ontological and above all temporal)
of potential with respect to the act. But do we have a solid basis for such a thesis? This is the question that we now face.
zh: 不过，迄今勾勒的论证仍然面临一个醒目难题——至少有一个尚未解决的问题。只有当非现在显得属于过去时，记忆才会同它打交道并描绘它。潜能根本的非现实性不足以证明记忆会汲取它，因为这种非现实性还必须采取过去的形式。请注意，只是形式；我们当然不是在谈年代性的“那时”。但即使如此，把一种官能的非现在认作“之前”，是否成立？即使这个“之前”不确定、没有日期，也无法附着到任何既定当下？断言潜能的非现实性具有过去的特征、因而可以被记忆，意味着断言潜能相对于实现具有绝对的在先性——逻辑的、本体论的，尤其是时间的在先性。但我们是否拥有支持这一命题的坚实基础？这就是现在面对的问题。
康德，‘经验的类比。第一类比：实体持存性原理’，见《纯粹理性批判》第二章，伦敦：麦克米伦，1958年，第214页。另见：‘现象的一切变化都必须在其中得到思考的时间，本身保持不变而且不会变化。因为只有在时间中，并且作为时间的规定，相继或共存才可能得到表象。’（第213页）
en: Kant, ‘Analogies of Experience. First Analogy: Principle of the Permanence of Substance’, Chapter II in

, London: Macmillan 1958, p. 214. Furthermore: ‘time, in which all changes of appearances has to be thought, remains and does not change. For it is that in which, and as determinations of which, succession or coexistence can alone be represented’ (p. 213).

zh: 同上，第214页。‘时间本身不能被知觉。因此，必须在知觉对象中，也就是在现象中，找到某种代表一般时间的基底；一切变化与共存必须在对这个基底的把握中，并通过现象同它的关系而得到知觉。但一切实在者——也就是一切属于事物存在者——的基底是实体；一切属于存在的东西只能被思考为实体的规定。因此，唯有同持存者的关系，才能规定现象的一切时间关系；这个持存者就是现象领域中的实体，也就是现象中的实在者，它作为一切变化的基底始终保持同一。’（同上，第213页）
en: Ibid, p. 214. ‘Now, time cannot by itself be perceived. Consequently there must be found in the object of perception, that is, in the appearances, the substratum which represents time in general; and all change and coexistence must, in being apprehended, be perceived in this substratum, and through relation of the appearances to it. But the substratum of all that is real, that is, of all that belongs to the existence of things, is substance; and all that belongs to existence can be thought only as a determination of substance. Consequently the permanent, in relation to which alone all time-relations of appearances can be determined, is substance in the [field of] appearance, that is, the real in appearance, and as the substrate of all change remains ever the same’ (Ibid., p. 213).

zh: 同上。在第一章中，康德已经勾勒这个问题的基本要项：‘实体的图式，是实在者在时间中的持存，也就是把实在者表象为一般经验性时间规定的基底，因而在其他一切变化时仍然保持。（短暂者的存在在时间中消逝，但时间本身并不消逝。时间自身非短暂且持存，在现象领域中与它相对应的，是其存在非短暂者，也就是实体。只有在同实体的关系中，现象的相继与共存才能在时间中得到规定。）’（同上，第184页）
en: Ibid. In Chapter I, Kant had already sketched out the essential terms of the question: ‘The schema of substance is the permanence of the real in time, that is, the representation of the real as a substrate of empirical determination of time in general, and so as abiding while all else changes. (The existence of what is transitory passes away in time but not time itself. To time, itself non-transitory and abiding, there corresponds in the [field of] appearance what is non-transitory in its existence, that is, substance. Only in [relation to] substance can the succession and coexistence of appearances be determined in time)’ (Ibid., p. 184).

zh: 同上。因此，本质上未实现的不是未来，而是时间总体；过去、当下和未来这些不同的年代维度，都在同时间总体的关系中得到分节。现象层面的明证——只有尚未充分展开完毕时才有时间——代表落入时间之物与时间总体之间的关系。但它以误导方式代表这种关系，因为两个领域只被划分成‘已经实现’与‘尚未实现’。作为整体的时间非但不是‘尚未’展开完毕，而且根本永远不受展开过程支配。落入时间之物则总采取现实性的形式：就连我们必须等待的未来，也无非是一种推迟的现实性。如果我们把未完成性——潜在性——归给未来，而它实际上属于作为整体的时间，那么几乎不可避免地会把未来选作时间性的承重轴，并误认它为构成性的‘本源时间’。关于当代哲学很大一部分中反复出现的类似张冠李戴，参见下文第二部分第11节‘死亡与历史’。
en: Ibid. What is essentially unrealised is not, then, the future, but rather the totality of time in relation to which the various different chronological dimensions are articulated: past, present and future. The phenomenal evidence – there is only time if it has not fully played out – represents the relation between that which falls
time and the ensemble
time. But it does so in a misleading way, since the two ambits are divided only into the
realised’ and the
realised’. Time-as-a-whole, far from being ‘not yet’ played out, is never subject to playing out at all. For its part, that which falls

time always takes the form of actuality: even the future we have to wait for is nothing other than a postponed actuality. If we attribute incompleteness – potentiality – to the future, when it instead belongs to time-as-a-whole, then it is more or less inevitable that we will choose the future as the load-bearing axis of temporality, mistaking it for the constitutive ‘originary time’. On a similar
recurrent across much of contemporary philosophy, see below, Part II,
section 11
, ‘Death and history’.
Ibid, p. 214.
